note: Context windows and output caps. Every entry names its source. Nothing here was measured by this project, so all of it is `vendor-doc`: read from vendor documentation on the checked date and not re-verified since. Override any of it with --window and --reserve rather than trusting a table that ages.

sources.vendor-doc: Vendor documentation, read on the checked date. A claim, not a measurement.
sources.shared-window: Local runtimes do not cap the reply separately. The reply comes out of the same window as the prompt, so the reserve here is a choice you are making and not a limit the runtime imposes.

gpt-4-turbo.note: 128k of window and 4k of reply. The reply cap binds long before the window does, and that is the case this tool exists to make visible.

claude.label: Claude
claude.why: Anthropic publishes no tokenizer. Counting Claude exactly needs the count_tokens API endpoint and a key. This tool uses the cl100k_base table as a stand-in and reports the count as unmeasured with no error band, because inventing a band would be worse than admitting there is none.

local_runtime_warning: Setting a long context on a local runtime is easy to get wrong. Measured on ollama 0.32.9 on the machine that built this: only `options.num_ctx` in the API request body changes the loaded context length. `/set parameter num_ctx` in the REPL and `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` in the client shell both leave the server default in place and report no error, so a run you believe has 128k may be truncating at the default. Check `ollama ps` for the loaded size.
